title: Design audit: phone and computer
eyebrow: Design for approval · audit of all seven screens · nothing built yet

short.lead: I ran the real app at phone size (390 by 844) and computer size (1440 by 900) with 8 projects, 56 tasks and 5 thoughts, and compared it with the screenshot you sent. Three things fall short of the goal: the screen is mostly empty, the task is not the biggest thing, and no screen shows the next step for each area and project.
short.hint: 'Today' pictures are the real app. 'Proposed' pictures are drawings with the same sample data.
items: On a computer, about a quarter of the window is used
On Focus the paper covers 23% of a 1440 by 900 window. The rest is blank desk. In your own screenshot the clipboard is a narrow column in a much wider window, and 18 Up next tasks scroll inside it.

items.alt: Today's Focus on a computer: a small clipboard in the middle of an empty window
items.caption: Focus today on a computer.

items: Focus asks two questions before it shows a task

Opening Focus shows 'Which project?' with 34 things to tap, then 'What kind of work?'. Only then does a task appear, and its Done stamp is the same size as the Another button. Nothing tells you what is next in your other projects.

items.alt: Today's Focus on a phone: a filing cabinet asking which project
items.caption: Focus today on a phone: a question, not an answer.

items: Focus opens on the task, with the next step of every area under it

One big yellow note is the thing to do now, already picked the way 'Pick for me' picks today. One big Done stamp. Under it, one small note per area shows that area's next step; tapping it opens that area's projects. The two questions move behind 'Choose…'.

items.alt: Proposed Focus on a phone: a big yellow note, a Done stamp, and four small area notes
items.caption: Proposed Focus on a phone.

items: On a computer the same screen uses the whole window
The big note sits on the left. On the right, every project shows its next step, in a column per area. Tapping a small note makes it the big one. Nothing is hidden behind a pick.

items.alt: Proposed Focus on a computer: big note on the left, a column of small notes per area on the right
items.caption: Proposed Focus on a computer.

items: Today there are stamps, flags, tape labels, brass handles and a '⋯' tag, and the brass handle has no word on it. Proposed: four shapes, each with one meaning, and every button carries a word.

items.alt: Legend: yellow note is a task, small coloured note is a next step, stamp is the main action, plain button is everything else
items.caption: The whole design language.

changes: chg
Roadmap on a computer
The four lists sit side by side like a board, and the first Up next task is a yellow note marked Next step.
One list at a time in a narrow clipboard
Four columns across the window
Each column shows a handful of tasks and a 'Show more' line, so a project with hundreds of done tasks stays calm. Dragging between columns works as it does today.

The six tabs, + Jot, sync, Settings, the Projects filing cabinet, Task details, dark mode and all your data.
The next-step pick reuses the order 'Pick for me' already uses (app/js/pick-order.js). No new data is stored.
choices: focus

A
The task, already picked, with next steps under it
As drawn. 'Choose…' still opens the two questions.
B
The two questions, as today, only bigger
Keeps the pick in your hands every time.
Opening on an answer removes the decision you can get stuck on; choosing is still one tap away.
notes

One per area; tap to see its projects
No more notes than you have areas.
B
One per project, in a scrolling list
Everything visible, but with 26 projects, as in your own data, that is 26 notes.
One per area keeps the screen short; a computer has room to show every project at once.

wrapup.summary: The audit found empty space, a task that is not the biggest thing, and no view of the next step per area and project. The proposal fixes those on Focus, Roadmap, Sort, Review and Organize with four shapes that each mean one thing.
wrapup.changing: Changed: the layout of Focus, Roadmap, Sort, Review and Organize on phone and computer. Not changed: tabs, data, Projects, Settings.
wrapup.blocking: Waiting on your five answers under Choices. Nothing is built until you approve.
wrapup.next: After approval: one main GitHub issue with a smaller issue for each screen, then the build in the order you pick, then one checking page with before and after pictures from the real app.
